messages:
devon: FYI ran a focused perf + profile sweep on continuous batching today. Goal: understand why short requests (<=64 tokens) are experiencing p95 latency spikes when a few tenants send long sequences (>1024). TL;DR: token-budget carryover + kernel-selection hysteresis are amplifying starvation across tenants.
sara: nice — what environment and workload mix?
devon: staging canary (dedicated pool). workload mix: ~70% short (<64), 30% long (>1024). Under load (concurrent tokens in queue > ~600) short p95 went from ~80ms -> ~240ms. throughput overall steady but latency tail for shorts bad.
mike: do you have flamegraphs or perf traces? my hunch: kernel switch cost + batching holdouts for long sequences.
devon: attached profiling excerpt (pasted below). key signals:
```
- kernel_switch_time: median 0.8ms, tail 12-18ms when switching to long-kernel
- batch_formation_delay: median 2.1ms, short-p95 180ms when backlog high
- kv_cache_evictions/sec: spikes correlated with long-seq bursts
```
config I used for the sweep:
```yaml
continuous_batcher:
  token_budget_target: 2048
  per_request_token_cap: 4096
  max_wait_ms: 120
  starvation_guard:
    enabled: true
    short_seq_priority_tokens: 256
```
(we were using kernel-selection policy: prefer kernels optimized for >512 tokens if avg_batch_tokens > 512)
anya: interesting. the kv_cache_evictions point is important — long sequences fill kv caches causing prefix miss rate for short requests to increase, which in turn makes their latencies worse.
sara: can we quantify the starvation across tenants vs across request lengths? is it one noisy tenant or many?
devon: mostly 2 tenants with sustained long sequences (streaming RLHF-ish workloads). when they hit sustained windows the scheduler accumulates token credits for them and the batcher waits to form large token-rich batches (to hit kernel sweet spots). that waiting creates queuing delay for short ones.
mike: proposals:
1) per-tenant token buckets (hard cap) with decay on idle so a single tenant can't hoard.
2) priority aging for short requests: if wait > X ms, bump to high priority for next N batches.
3) kernel hysteresis: avoid switching to long-token kernel unless we expect next M batches to sustain long token counts (predictive threshold).
4) kv-cache prefetch/partition: reserve a small fast cache partition for short prefixes.

devon: ran quick A/B on 1+2 combined: results — short p95 improved from 240ms -> 110ms, overall throughput dropped ~5% (due to loss of batching efficiency for long seqs). cpu/gpu utilization similar.
anya: that's promising. we should document acceptable trade-offs: lower short tail vs small throughput hit. production SLOs probably prefer latency for short interactive requests.
sara: agreed. let's also add an opt-in per-tenant QoS flag (interactive:true) customers can set, default off.
mike: also consider dynamic token_budget_target that adapts by sampled request length distribution over 30s windows rather than static 2048. that might let us regain some throughput.
devon: added one more observation: kernel-switch overhead was exaggerated by small batches that triggered heavy memcpy + kernel reconfigure. adding a tiny batch-size floor (>=128 tokens) for switching avoided the worst of the 12-18ms tails.
infra-bot: canary deployment of batcher-v2 with tenant-buckets and priority-aging finished at 2026-03-17T09:24:00Z :white_check_mark:

anya: next steps I propose:
- schedule multi-tenant canary with 2 long-seq tenants + synthetic short traffic (A/B: baseline vs tenant-buckets+aging+kernel-hysteresis)
- add temp metrics: per-tenant token_hold_time, short_wait_50/95, kernel_switch_count
- KV cache experiment: reserve 10% partition for short-prefix hot set and measure miss rate

sara: I'll schedule the canary. devon/mike, can you own the rollout and dashboards?
devon: yep will own rollout + dashboards. putting quick dashboard tiles for short_p95, kernel_switch_ms, kv_evictions.
mike: I'll work on predictive kernel threshold logic and simulate with the replay tool.
anya: chic. let's aim for canary tomorrow morning and reconvene after run. :thumbsup:
